notes.title: Prologue. Part 3
notes.content:
The chair next to him was empty again. He glanced at watches and got up heavily to his feet. Two girls rushed past him. An elderly man in a torn jacket, barely dodging them, walked in the opposite direction. Captain sighed. He won't see any other people in the coming weeks besides his pilot. Then, they will spend a few days in a small remote station. And the way back will take even longer.

He walked leisurely towards the airlock, bypassing groups of talking people and giving a way for those who were in a hurry. There were less than 20 steps to the airlock when someone's hand blocked his way.

"Need to deliver a cargo to Mars? Faster than official carriers." the woman said in a low voice. She looked into Capitan's eyes, and he looked at his recent neighbor.

"Ah," she said with disappointment. "You are departing. "

Сaptain nodded.

"By the way, what happened with the big cargo ship which arrived at the station a couple of hours ago?" captain asked.

"Their pilot fell asleep." the woman dropped andю She lost all interest to Captain and stepped aside.

notes.title: Prologue. Part 2
notes.content:
Not only the captain drew attention to the strange transport. The station's outer spotlights flashed orange. Obeying the request of the automatic dispatcher, the ship going to dock lit up like a light bulb in a dark room. The captain shuddered: even the most powerful gravitational compensators will not save him from overload, which would be caused by such a sharp activation of the main engines.

"Bloody reckless pilots!" an elderly woman, sitting to the left of the captain, exclaimed. She throwed her keychain on the floor and stood up. "Don't they even try to ask for a discount."

The transporter began to flyby maneuver above the station and disappeared from view.

A guy in blue overalls plopped down on the chair next to the captain.

"Did you see that?" he exclaimed. "I bet something happened on that ship."
"A bad pilot happened, I presume." the captain remarked.
"C'mon. We are on the border of outer space! Anything can happen here. They were in such a hurry, as if they were escaping from something. Or from someone, can you imagine? And what if the someone is on their ship? Maybe we should isolate ourselves on the Walrus, before it's too late?"

The captain ignored his pilot's fantasies.

"Have you prepared for the flight?" he asked. "I sent you a cargo mass summary half an hour ago."
"Really? I seem to have missed the message. I met my friend here. Guess what, he returned from Enceladus last week..."

Captain yawned. He did not dislike his pilot. Rather, even he liked this guy. Especially when his mouth was closed.

"He have only four days on Mars, and then have to go again to the outer system. This is life! If I could too..."

Captain closed his eyes. Captain opened his eyes.

notes.title: Prologue. Part 1
notes.content:
Mars-4 transport station needs a renovations desperately. About 10 years ago, the government of the Martian colony succumbed to numerous business demands and built new transport hub to ease-off the main station. Although, it didn't help much. The new station clearly failed to cope with intense stream of cargo moving to the Mars surface and in the opposite direction. Years later, they'd say even a private mini-station near the outer planets looks like a mansions comparing to Mars-4.

Captain closed the door of the customs office behind, and immediately found himself in the wailing crowd. Hi resisted firmly the desire to push people aside, and made his way into the waiting room. After a moment of hesitation, he took a chair by the window and stretched out his legs with relief. A seat at the left was occupied by an elderly but sturdy, unkempt woman, twirling a broken keychain in her hands. Captain glanced at her with dislike and sighed. Only two hours to wait, and he'll leave this place. Two hours: that is how long it takes for robotic loaders to secure the cargo on the external sling of the White Walrus, his spaceship.

Mars — one of the most industrialized planets of the solar system — was clearly visible outside the window at a distance of more than 9 thousand kilometers. A chain of three cargo ships stretched from the station in a direction of the planet. To their left a huge transport flew up to the station. In space, it is difficult to estimate by eye speed and direction of objects, but something unnatural in this ship caught the captain's attention. A huge lump, lined with metal, not less than 20 meters high. On its board, he barely read the numbers: 2264. This is probably a year built. Such large ships are usually used in the outer solar system, because this is just commercially unfeasible to send small transport ships there. And this is not always possible, given how much fuel such flight takes.

Suddenly the captain realized what's wrong with this ship. It was further from the station than it seemed at first. And therefore the transporter was moving very quickly. Much faster than it should.
